content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part**: A single sugarcane leaf, shown laid flat against a light background
- **Overall color**: Pale/light green to yellowish-green throughout the entire blade — suggesting systemic disease
- **Key lesion**: A distinct reddish-maroon to dark pink streak running along the central midrib area of the leaf
- **Texture/pattern**: The reddish discoloration is concentrated along the central vein/midrib; the rest of the blade is uniformly pale green

**Reasoning through candidate classes:**

- **Yellow_Leaf** (Yellow Leaf Syndrome / ScYLV): Classic symptoms include (1) overall yellowing/pale color of the leaf blade and (2) a characteristic pink-to-red discoloration of the **midrib**, especially visible on the abaxial (underside) surface. The image shows exactly this — pale, yellowish-green lamina with a vivid reddish-maroon midrib stripe. This is a textbook presentation.
- **Leaf_Scald**: Typically shows white/cream pencil-line stripes along the leaf margins or blade, not reddish midrib discoloration.
- **Brown_Spot**: Would show discrete oval/eye-shaped lesions with straw-colored centers, not a continuous midrib streak.
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus / Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: Would show green/yellow mosaic or streak patterns, not reddish midrib.
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: Associated with distorted growing points and chlorotic twisting, not this pattern.
- **Yellow_Spot**: Yellow discoloration in spots, not reddish midrib streaking.

The combination of **generalized pale/yellow lamina + vivid reddish-pink midrib streak** is highly characteristic of Yellow Leaf Syndrome in sugarcane.
